issues.legal_issue: The notice to quit satisfied the applicable legal requirements in the circumstances of the eviction proceeding.
material_facts: The case was an appeal by a landlord in eviction proceedings.
The landlord had succeeded in three courts, including before a single judge of the High Court.
The Division Bench reversed on the sole question of whether the notice to quit was valid.
The Supreme Court agreed with the single judge that, in the circumstances of the case, the notice complied with the law; the judgment does not state the notice’s terms.
issues.conclusion: The notice to quit was valid, and the appeal was allowed, subject to the modification concerning recovery of possession.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the notice to quit complied with the law in the circumstances of the case. The judgment identifies no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for that conclusion.

predicates.appeal_in_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought an appeal arising from eviction proceedings.
predicates.division_bench_reversed_on_notice_validi: A Division Bench reversed the lower-court result on the validity of the notice to quit.
predicates.notice_complied_with_law_in_case_circums: The notice to quit satisfied the applicable legal requirements in the circumstances of the case.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal concerns a Division Bench reversal on notice validity and the notice satisfies the legal requirements in the circumstances, the notice is valid.

issues.legal_issue: Recovery of possession may be postponed and conditioned on undertakings when the tenant has been conducting business in the premises.
material_facts: The tenant had been conducting business for some years in the shop subject to the eviction proceedings.
The Court directed that the landlord not recover possession until the end of 1977, and the tenant undertook to surrender possession by then.
The landlord undertook to give the tenant the first option to rent any part of the building that was let, at fair rent, before letting it to someone else.
The tenant undertook not to obstruct reconstruction so long as possession was not interfered with and the shop’s walls or roof were not damaged.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed subject to postponing recovery of possession and recording the parties’ undertakings concerning surrender, a first option to rent, and reconstruction.
issues.legal_principle: The Court, having regard to the tenant’s ongoing business in the shop, ordered a temporary postponement of recovery of possession and recorded the parties’ undertakings. The judgment identifies no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this direction.

rule.if: eviction_appeal and tenant_has_conducted_business_in_premises and tenant_undertakes_to_surrender and landlord_undertakes_first_rental_option and tenant_undertakes_not_to_obstruct_safe_reconstruction

predicates.eviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from an eviction case.
predicates.tenant_has_conducted_business_in_premise: The tenant has conducted business for some time in the premises subject to eviction.
predicates.tenant_undertakes_to_surrender: The tenant undertakes to surrender possession by the end of the permitted period.
predicates.landlord_undertakes_first_rental_option: The landlord undertakes to give the tenant the first option to rent premises that are offered for rent, at fair rent, before renting them to someone else.
predicates.tenant_undertakes_not_to_obstruct_safe_r: The tenant undertakes not to obstruct reconstruction while possession is undisturbed and the premises are not damaged.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal involves a tenant who has conducted business in the premises and the parties give the stated undertakings, recovery of possession is postponed subject to those undertakings.
